summary: Architecture-only phase (no production code, no parser implementation, no regex replacement, no runtime change). Independently inventoried every Phase ID parsing/grammar/comparison implementation across src/pcae/: found fifteen distinct definitions across ten files, more than four times the three named in the governing brief (core/phase_reports.py, commands/push.py, core/repository_transition_integration.py), confirming the prior truncation-repair sequence was chasing an architectural defect (no single component owns Phase ID grammar) rather than a series of unrelated one-off bugs. Defined a canonical EBNF grammar derived independently from observed historical forms (the union of all fifteen consumers' accepted inputs), canonical parser responsibilities and boundaries, canonical representation and normalization semantics, comparison semantics generalizing the existing branch-aware, not-always-comparable ordering rule rather than replacing it, a closed error taxonomy, a per-consumer lifecycle-integration table covering all ten files, a non-flag-day migration strategy, and compatibility/extensibility/security/risk sections. Noted the repository-transition-integration text-scanning helper as the one inventoried consumer still carrying an unrepaired instance of the truncation defect at the time of this phase (flagged, not fixed -- out of this architecture-only phase's scope). Runtime remained Observed / observe / unavailable throughout.
tests_added_or_updated: None -- architecture-only phase, no production code and no test authored or modified. Full untargeted suite run twice for regression confirmation: with this phase's docs-only changes applied, and again against unmodified main after a git stash of those changes, to independently confirm no new failure was introduced.
